evidence.claim: Developed a patented time-domain wave-equation datuming algorithm that upward continues borehole data to the topographic surface, bypassing Pre-Stack Depth Migration (PSDM) complexities [1.2.2].
Deploys Pre-stack Depth Imaging using proprietary reflection tomography combined with state-of-the-art Tsunami Kirchhoff-based depth imaging tools [1.2.3].
Pairs Landmark's SeisSpace® ProMAX® software with proprietary high-frequency enhancement algorithms to extend usable seismic frequencies near the VibroSeis sweep limit [1.3.3, 1.4.2].
Houses an on-premise hardware infrastructure equipped with over 4,400 computing cores and 480TB of dedicated storage [1.3.3].
Leverages internal parallel processing clusters to expedite run-times for data-driven reflection tomography and Kirchhoff depth migrations [1.2.3].
Focuses operations strictly on third-party contract data processing and custom reprocessing workflows rather than building or brokering a speculative multi-client library [1.1.2, 1.2.8].

Acts as a downstream processor for external libraries, as demonstrated by legal case records highlighting their handling of licensed data belonging to dedicated brokers like Silverthorne Seismic [1.3.7].

Supports long-term 4D time-lapse monitoring setups for carbon capture (CCUS) projects, including the successful processing of a 5-survey time-lapse 3D VSP to monitor subsurface CO2 injection [1.5.1, 1.5.2].

Provides DASeis™ Distributed Acoustic Sensing Imaging technology, processing horizontal wellbore DAS fiber optic records to map time-lapse reservoir dynamics like pore pressure shifts and fracture density variations [1.2.1].

Engaged in US Department of Energy (NETL) funded geomechanical research alongside Battelle, using random-forest machine learning (ML) models to predict triaxial wave velocities from experimental data [2.2.6].

Standard commercial delivery continues to rely primarily on deterministic workflows and conventional physics-based geophysics suites (e.g., OMNI™ and VizPRO) rather than productized, automated AI interpretation engines [2.2.9, 2.3.16].

Legal case documents show that Casillas Petroleum Resource Partners II, L.L.C. contracted with Sterling Seismic Services, Ltd. for data processing.
Court records indicate a multi-party data processing and licensing arrangement involving Silverthorne Seismic, LLC and Sterling Seismic Services.

Project documentation reveals that Sterling Seismic Services, Ltd. was contracted to process and interpret data for the South Railroad Project alongside Bird Seismic Services and Columbia Geophysical.
Sterling's main office and primary data processing facility is located at 8020 Shaffer Parkway, Suite 100, Littleton, Colorado, USA.
Industry directories and corporate historical filings indicate that Sterling has maintained a satellite processing center office at 11767 Katy Freeway, Houston, Texas, USA.
Corporate intelligence records via RocketReach estimate Sterling Seismic Services, Ltd.'s private revenue at approximately $6.2 million.
Internal company data confirms that Sterling has a long-term backlog of performance, having reprocessed more than 28,000 land seismic projects across major US basins over three decades.
Client portfolios from industry technical consultants show an integrated services relationship between iReservoir.com and Sterling Seismic Services Ltd..

Technical workflows listed by the company show active algorithmic collaborations for 5D regularization and high-dimensional Fourier processing, though specific software licensing alliance brands are kept proprietary.

Industry reporting from Stellar Market Research explicitly classifies Sterling Seismic Services Ltd. as a minor, niche boutique player in the North American Seismic Service market compared to majors like Schlumberger and CGG.

The company manages over 4,400 computing cores and 480TB of storage in-house, highlighting a small single-digit regional market infrastructure share relative to multinational tier-1 seismic compute clouds.
